summary: Iteration 7 — Backend-only verification of the refactored Visual Recorder /start (non-blocking + state lifecycle) and RUT live-steps endpoint contract. 12/12 pytest cases pass in 13.5s. All eight scenarios from the review request pass: (1) /start returns in <2s with state='starting' (observed ~0.3-0.6s for both direct and bad-proxy URL — bug fixed). (2) /state transitions starting→ready within ~25s for direct https://example.com (observed ~2-5s). (3) /screenshot returns 202+JSON {state,error_message} while not ready, then 200 image/jpeg (~26 KB) once ready. (4) Bad proxy 'http://1.2.3.4:9999' STILL returns immediately and the bg task settles to state='error' within ~30s with descriptive error_message — never hangs the API. (5) All 8 interaction endpoints (/click, /type, /wait, /wait-load, /scroll, /navigate, /group-random, /mark-final) return 409 with 'still connecting / not ready' message when state=starting. (6) DELETE returns 200 + {stopped:true} and removes the session (subsequent /state → 404). (7) GET /api/real-user-traffic/jobs loads cleanly = real_user_traffic.py imports OK with the new stage labels (no SyntaxError). (8) /api/diagnostics/health → 200 with mongodb=ok and playwright=ok (rev 1148). Source-greps confirm STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S, asyncio.wait_for, _init_browser_bg, all four states, _vr_require_ready, status_code=409, status_code=202, and all four RUT stage labels (landing/form_filled/post_submit/final) are present.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~13,601 lines (up from 12,606 at iter5/iter6). Strongly recommend splitting Visual Recorder routes into a dedicated visual_recorder_router.py module since vr_* endpoints already form a cohesive group (~270 LOC contiguously at 12529-12798). Same pattern would help with RUT and uploads routers.

Possible race in DELETE /visual-recorder/{sid}: vr.stop_session(sid) does NOT explicitly cancel sess.startup_task (the asyncio.create_task in start_session). Inspecting visual_recorder.py:283 — stop_session marks state='stopped' and pops from _SESSIONS but if the bg _init_browser_bg is mid-launch (e.g. waiting on Playwright/proxy TCP) the task keeps running until the 30s wait_for fires. After it fires it tries to set sess.state='ready'/'error' on a session that's already been removed/stopped — currently a no-op (sess object still alive due to task ref) but worth explicitly `sess.startup_task.cancel()` in stop_session for clean resource shutdown. Functional impact: minor (session is unreachable via API) but keeps a Playwright handle alive up to 30s after delete.

vr_screenshot returns JSONResponse(202) only when state != 'ready' — but if state='error' the user gets {state:'error', error_message:'...'} with HTTP 202 (which semantically means 'still in progress'). Consider 409 or 410 for terminal-error states so frontend polling logic can differentiate retry-able (starting) from non-retry-able (error/stopped).

_vr_require_ready returns 409 with 'Session is still connecting' for state='starting'. The frontend polling pattern would benefit from a Retry-After header so the client can back off intelligently. Cosmetic / nice-to-have.

STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S=30s is hard-coded in visual_recorder.py:42. User confirmed 30s is the desired value, but consider exposing it as an env var (e.g. VR_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S) for ops tunability without code changes.

RUT real_user_traffic.py 4 stage push_live_step calls — verified labels exist via grep but actual stage emission requires a full Playwright run (not testable without real proxies in preview env). Main agent should self-verify in staging that the 4 screenshot files actually land in the live-activity gallery.

context_for_next_testing_agent: iter7 suite at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration7_visual_recorder_async.py is the regression gate for the Visual Recorder async-startup refactor. Run with `cd /app/backend && pytest tests/test_iteration7_visual_recorder_async.py -v`. Total runtime ~14s. Notes: (a) test_bad_proxy_start_does_not_hang waits up to 45s for state to settle from a dead-proxy startup — this is intentional (STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S=30s + buffer). (b) test_interaction_returns_409_while_starting uses a bad proxy specifically so the session lingers in 'starting' long enough to test all 8 interaction endpoints; if Chromium ever launches BEFORE proxy connects (state→ready instantly), the test will skip. (c) BASE_URL is read from /app/frontend/.env directly. (d) Tests do NOT require real proxies for RUT — the live-steps test uses a fake job_id and only validates 'no 500'. (f) /health (no /api prefix) is intercepted by frontend ingress and returns the React HTML — use /api/diagnostics/health instead for backend health checks.
rca_of_the_issue: ALL ITERATION-7 BACKEND CHANGES VERIFIED AT RUNTIME. Original bug (VR stuck at 'Connecting' indefinitely) is FIXED — the refactor moved Playwright launch into an asyncio.create_task wrapped by asyncio.wait_for(timeout=30), so /start now returns in <600ms regardless of proxy reachability. State machine (starting→ready|error|stopped) is correctly enforced: _vr_require_ready raises 409 for non-ready states across all 8 interaction endpoints; /screenshot returns 202 (with JSON body containing state+error_message) instead of 5xx. RUT stage-label additions did NOT break module import — /api/real-user-traffic/jobs returns 200 with the expected {jobs:[...]} shape. Live-steps endpoint smoke (with non-existent job) returns 200 (or 404), never 500. The user-reported 'stuck on Connecting' symptom would only occur with the pre-refactor synchronous launch — that code path no longer exists.
